summary.es: Suelo, luz, cielo, PlayerStart y NavMesh en el nivel abierto, listo para darle a Play.
summary.en: Floor, light, sky, PlayerStart and NavMesh in the open level, ready to press Play.
summary.zh-CN: 在当前打开的关卡中放置地面、灯光、天空、PlayerStart 和 NavMesh，可以直接点击 Play。

recipes.steps: Build a test level in the level that is open now; reuse what already exists instead of duplicating it. 1) Floor: one large flat StaticMeshActor with collision at Z = 0, labeled DBV_Floor (for example /Engine/BasicShapes/Cube scaled to (50, 50, 0.2) and placed so its top is at Z = 0). 2) A DirectionalLight. 3) A sky: SkyAtmosphere plus a SkyLight with real-time capture, unless the level already has a sky. 4) A PlayerStart about 100 cm above the floor. 5) A NavMeshBoundsVolume that covers the floor: give it the floor location and half-extent, never the size of the whole level. Put the new actors in the World Outliner folder DBV/TestLevel.

title.zh-CN: 带动画的 Tripo 角色

summary.es: Un modelo humanoide de Tripo con esqueleto y animaciones, montado en un Character Blueprint.
summary.en: A humanoid Tripo model with a skeleton and animations, set up in a Character Blueprint.
summary.zh-CN: 一个带骨骼和动画的人形 Tripo 模型，设置在 Character 蓝图中。

recipes.steps: Make a playable character from a Tripo model. 1) Pick a humanoid model in the library (library_list) or, only if the user agrees to the cost, generate one standing in an A-pose. 2) Rig it with rig_model and add idle, walk and run animations with animate_model (tell the user the price first; they cost credits). 3) Send the rigged model and its animations to Unreal with library_send_to_unreal. 4) Create a Character Blueprint under /Game/DBV/Blueprints whose Mesh component uses the rigged Skeletal Mesh, turned -90 degrees in yaw and lowered by half the capsule height so the feet touch the ground. 5) Optionally make it the default pawn. Compile and save the Blueprint.

title.es: Caminar por un mundo de World Labs
title.en: Walk through a World Labs world
title.zh-CN: 漫步 World Labs 世界

summary.es: Un mundo de la biblioteca colocado a escala con su colisión y el PlayerStart sobre el terreno, para recorrerlo en Play.
summary.en: A library world placed at scale with its collision and the PlayerStart on the terrain, to walk through it in Play.
summary.zh-CN: 把资源库中的一个世界按真实比例放入关卡，带碰撞，并把 PlayerStart 放在地面上，在 Play 中走一走。

recipes.steps: Let the user walk through a World Labs world. 1) Choose a world in the library (library_list, kind "world"); generate one with generate_world only if the user agrees to the cost. 2) Send it with library_send_to_unreal: the app places the Gaussian splat at metric scale with the ground at Z = 0, aligns its collision mesh and lifts a PlayerStart that was under the terrain. 3) Make sure there is a PlayerStart standing on the collision (move it above the ground if needed) and that the level has a playable character (the project default pawn is fine). 4) Tell the user to press Play and walk.

title.zh-CN: 用 Convai 说话的 MetaHuman

summary.es: Un MetaHuman en el nivel con su personaje de Convai, el jugador preparado para hablar y la NavMesh para moverse.
summary.en: A MetaHuman in the level with its Convai character, the player ready to talk and the NavMesh to move.
summary.zh-CN: 关卡中的 MetaHuman 配上它的 Convai 角色，玩家可以对话，并有用于移动的 NavMesh。

recipes.steps: Make a MetaHuman talk with Convai. 1) Read the Convai skills first: ListSkills and GetSkills of ToolsetRegistry.AgentSkillToolset. 2) Place the assembled MetaHuman Blueprint (/Game/MetaHumans/<Name>/BP_<Name>), not the MetaHumanCharacter asset. 3) Ask which Convai character to use (convai_characters lists the registered ones) and run SetupConvaiCharacter with its Character ID. 4) Run SetupConvaiPlayer on the player pawn. 5) Add a NavMeshBoundsVolume sized to the walkable floor (AddNavMeshVolumeForCurrentLevel with the floor location and half-extent). 6) Optionally name places with level_zones_propose so the character can be asked to go there. Remind the user that the conversation happens in Play, with the microphone.

summary.es: Medir lo que pasa mientras juegas, cruzarlo con lo que notas y confirmar la causa antes de tocar nada.
summary.en: Measure what happens while you play, cross it with what you notice and confirm the cause before changing anything.
summary.zh-CN: 在你游玩时测量发生的事情，与你的感受交叉对照，在修改任何东西之前先确认原因。

recipes.steps: Diagnose a failure that happens while the game runs (movement, physics, jitter, collisions, animation, timing, something that happens 'sometimes') by MEASURING before changing anything. 1) Reproduce: ask the user what they noticed and when. Propose a short plan with session_plan (what to record and what the user should do), show it, and record with session_start while the user plays (the chat is busy, so the user marks moments and finishes with the buttons of the recording panel in the app; session_wait follows them until it returns finished); if they wear a headset, never ask them to look at the screen. A recording or a playtest in PIE does not replace the user's own play with the headset: say so. 2) Measure: stop with session_stop and cross what the user felt with the data (session_analyze: read gaps first, and if the measurement is not reliable say so and repeat with the editor in front; session_query shows the moments it points to) and answer as a table: what you noticed / what the data says / conclusion. Say what you measured and what you did not. 3) Isolate: if several causes remain, ask the user to switch ONE system off only for the test (session_isolate is not available yet) and record again. 4) Fix only what you confirmed, with the smallest change, reviewed by the user. 5) Validate: play again, compare session_analyze of this recording with the previous one (session_compare is not available yet) and check the log shows no new errors. 6) Remember: if the data contradicts a note in the project memory or a code comment, say so and propose correcting it. Never record with per-frame callbacks (register_slate_post_tick_callback, tick hooks) in unreal_run_python: they can outlive Play and flood the log.
